body.statement: Let \((q_n)\) be iid allocation vectors with \(q_n\to q^\star\). Uniformly whenever \(\zeta_n=n^{1/6}(q_n-q^\star)\) ranges over a compact subset of \(\{v:v_1+v_2+v_3=0\}\), \[\rho_n^{\mathrm{iid}}(q_n)=\frac1n+n^{-4/3}\{\mathsf P(\zeta_n)-C_3\}+o(n^{-4/3}).\] Hence an iid allocation array retains the unrestricted sharp correction \(C_3\) if and only if \(n^{1/6}(q_n-q^\star)\to0\). If \(q_n\to q^\star\) and \(n^{1/6}\|q_n-q^\star\|\to\infty\), then \(n^{4/3}\{\rho_n^{\mathrm{iid}}(q_n)-n^{-1}\}\to\infty\). The penalty \(\mathsf P(\zeta)=2\zeta_1^2+4\zeta_2^2+4\zeta_3^2\) is the constrained Hessian of \(q\mapsto\frac14\sum_ac_a^2/q_a\), and the displayed expansion proves its uniform coupling to the half-wedge experiment.
body.justification: This necessary-and-sufficient frontier turns the design into a first-class object and quantifies exactly when allocation error erases the second-order minimax gain.
body.gap: Bai (2023, Theorems 3.1--3.3) gives a first-order quadratic allocation result for linear procedures, while Zhao and Ding (2023) hold limiting multi-arm proportions fixed; neither derives the \(n^{-1/6}\) threshold or couples it to nonlinear minimax risk.
body.consumer: A multi-arm trial can translate the theorem into an allocation-tolerance rule: deviations smaller than \(n^{-1/6}\) preserve the sharp gain, while local deviations incur the explicit penalty.
